chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman, who said:
I asked Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about the person in Ihram who feels cold in his ears and covers them; he said: 'No'.

key_terms.أَبُو الْحَسَنِ: Abu Al-Hasan (Imam al-Rida, peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration)

ai.seo_question: Can a person in Ihram cover their ears if they feel cold?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies that covering the ears does not invalidate the Ihram state, distinguishing them from the head and face which are explicitly restricted. This ruling reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the prohibition applies specifically to the 'head' (including the top and sides) and the 'face' (including the area between the chin and eyebrows), while the ears remain exempt. The brevity of the answer underscores the precision of fiqh in distinguishing between covered and uncovered parts of the body during ritual consecration.

en.hubeali: Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abdul Rahman who said,
‘I asked Abu Al Hassanasws about the one in Ihraam feeling the cold in his ears, can he cover them both?’ Heasws said: ‘No’.
en.sarwar: 4. Abu Ali al-Ash’ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from Safwan from ‘Abd al-Rahman who has said the following:
“I once asked abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who because of cold covers his ears while in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘No, he must not do so.’”
